phaseTokens.night: moon ink, dark glass, brighter accent/gain/loss/sun, color-scheme dark, black shadow base.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Lit blue pill for the one main action inside the sheet.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { height: 44px; padding: 0 20px; border: 0; border-radius: 9999px; color: #fff; font: 600 0.9375rem/1.375rem 'Geist Variable', system-ui, sans-serif; letter-spacing: -0.005em; background: linear-gradient(180deg, #4f8dff 0%, #2563eb 100%); box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgb(255 255 255 / 0.35), 0 1px 2px rgb(23 73 196 / 0.3), 0 10px 24px -10px rgb(37 99 235 / 0.7); transition: transform 0.4s cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1), filter 0.2s; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { filter: brightness(1.06); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: scale(0.965); transition-duration: 0.12s; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #2563eb; outline-offset: 2px; }

narrative.northStar: The Window Seat Under a Living Sky
narrative.overview:
The whole app sits under a full-bleed sky whose gradient, sun or moon, clouds and stars follow local time through four phases: dawn, day, golden and night. The phase is set on the root element (`html[data-sky]`) and every ink, glass and accent token re-resolves from it. The sky is the ground; working content rises over it on frosted glass sheets, and the things worth looking at (trips) are framed as aircraft cabin windows.

Density is calm and phone-first: one primary figure per view, set large and light, with money always tabular and always worded ("You owe", "You get back"). Depth is glass over sky, never flat white. Colour comes from the sky itself; the only saturated UI colour is the luminous blue of primary actions plus gain, loss and sun tones for meaning.
keyCharacteristics: Living sky backdrop in four phases, crossfading on change.
Frosted content sheet (34px top radius) that rises on every navigation.
Cabin Window frame with a drawn shade and a sky-and-cloud fallback in place of any missing photo.
Ultralight headline numerals that count up; Geist Mono reserved for codes and printed artefacts.
Authored, dimensional icons for categories and navigation; Phosphor (bold, duotone, fill) for UI actions.

rules.name: The Phase Token Rule
rules.body: UI colour is read from phase tokens on `html[data-sky]`, never hard-coded per screen. A colour that does not change between day and night is either cloud white, the navy used on white pills, or a mistake.

rules.name: The Sky Supplies the Colour Rule
rules.body: Gradients belong to the sky, to sky fallbacks inside windows, and to lit pills. No decorative gradient blobs elsewhere.

rules.name: The Worded Money Rule
rules.body: Gain and loss colours support a sentence ("You owe", "Owed", "All square"); they never carry meaning alone.

rules.name: The Light Numeral Rule
rules.body: Headline numbers are set extralight or light and large; labels around them stay semibold and small. Never bold a hero figure.

rules.name: The Mono Is Print Rule
rules.body: Geist Mono appears only where a real artefact would be printed: codes, tickets, receipts, links.

rules.name: The Lit Edge Rule
rules.body: Every glass surface carries a one-pixel bright inner top edge; it is what makes glass read as glass on a moving sky.

rules.name: The Four Glasses Rule
rules.body: Pick the material by where it sits: sheet on the sky as ground, panel inside the sheet, glass-control for pills on the sky, glass-bar for anything floating over content.

dos: Do set type placed directly on the sky with the sky text styles (white with an atmospheric shadow; 92% white for secondary), so it holds when a cloud drifts behind it.
Do put pill controls and strips on the sky in the glass-control material, so white labels keep 4.5:1 in every phase; use the white pill for the one primary action on the sky.

Do keep the luminary clear of controls and titles: on phones the sun or moon sits just above the top edge so only its rim and glow show; from 1024px it is shown whole in the open sky at the top right.
Do read every UI colour from the phase tokens and check new surfaces in all four phases, night included.
Do frame trip imagery in the cabin Window and rely on its sky fallback rather than a placeholder or broken image.
Do word every balance ("You owe", "You get back", "All square") and set amounts in tabular figures.
Do honour reduced motion for every new animation.
donts: Don't use em dashes in copy.
Don't use emoji as icons, and don't substitute a thin line-icon set for categories or navigation; those use the authored dimensional set.
Don't place navy ink or unshadowed white text directly on the sky.
Don't add decorative gradient blobs; colour comes from the sky.
Don't lay content on a flat opaque white page; working content sits on the frosted sheet.
Don't add uppercase eyebrow labels above headings; the only tracked uppercase in the world belongs to printed artefacts (the PAID stamp, receipt headers).
Don't use Geist Mono for interface labels or headings.
